A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GATEKEEPER, with matching core methods, benchmark families, and twelve figures. The main text, mathematics, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-classification, language-model, and vision-language experiments in Figures 4–7, plus additional analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and appendix analyses, and additionally reports an empirical check of model dominance in Section 3.1.

M1.justification: The evaluated two-model loss and inference gate remain unchanged. Appendix B.5 newly proposes a hierarchical cascade with stage-specific alpha values and downstream training on previously deferred inputs; this extension remains unevaluated. Section 3.2 also introduces teacher-generated soft targets as an alternative.

E1.justification: The same image-classification, language reasoning/question-answering, and vision-language classification/captioning datasets are evaluated. Deeper cascades and combinations with other inference techniques are discussed prospectively, without additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains Narasimhan et al. (2022), and Figure 6 retains Gupta et al. (2024), Reduce Confidence, and Answer “N”, alongside the untuned baselines. The calibration objectives and early-exit methods newly discussed in the appendix are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The evaluated model pairs, alpha sweeps, confidence rules, and metrics are retained. v3 provides more information about initial checkpoints and the common fine-tuning protocol, but does not establish a change to the existing experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 3.1 adds a brief empirical dominance diagnostic, reporting no small-model-correct/large-model-incorrect cases across the tasks. The existing alpha sensitivity, ROC, confidence-overlap, and fixed-deferral analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The new checklist states that all reported results are means over five random runs; v2 provides no corresponding run-count statement. This is newly disclosed averaging information, not evidence of increased runs, and it adds no variance estimates or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports empirical delta = 0 across all tasks in Section 3.1. The benchmark values and trends in Figures 4–7 and the appendix plots are retained, including the results underlying the redrawn Figures 5 and 7.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces informal dominance language with an explicit probability bound permitting rare counterexamples. Section 3.2 adds an O(NC) computation argument. The existing loss, gating, metric, and ideal-deferral formulas remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central confidence-tuning and cross-architecture deferral claims are retained. The conclusion newly asserts applicability to multi-stage cascades, broadening the stated scope, while Appendix B.5 explicitly leaves empirical validation of that extension to future work.

C2.justification: v3 adds the limitation that evaluation covers only two-model cascades and discusses potential composition with deeper cascades, speculative decoding, and early exits. Appendix B.4 adds comparative explanations of the masked loss. Existing utility, semantic-correctness, model-family, and factuality-judge limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly explains single-pass, vectorized minibatch computation with dynamically computed correctness masks and clarifies checkpoint initialization and shared baseline training. The checklist explicitly states that code is not being provided. These disclosures do not establish changed implementations or withdrawal of previously available code.

R1.justification: New Appendices B.1.5, B.1.6, and B.4 substantially expand positioning against speculative decoding, early exiting, and canonical calibration objectives. Added references include Guo et al. (2017), Lin et al. (2017), Pereyra et al. (2017), and Teerapittayanon et al. (2016); publication-metadata updates to retained works are separate.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and expanded. Training is reorganized into a prerequisite followed by fine-tuning and inference stages, and new background subsections and a conference checklist expand the document structure.

P2.justification: The two-column workshop format becomes a largely single-column conference layout, with extensive figure relocation and equation/caption reformatting. Figure 1's schematic is rearranged, Figure 5's panels become vertically stacked, and Figure 7's proportions and ticks change. All twelve figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through implementation explanations, five-run disclosure, and clearer discussion of scope. However, its new assertion that approximate dominance guarantees no expected accuracy loss does not follow when delta is positive (Section 3.1), and Appendix B.4's positive entropy penalty conflicts with its stated flattening effect. With benchmark evidence unchanged, these gains and newly introduced technical problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
